stories.title: Almost half of world’s farmers poisoned by pesticides every year, experts find
stories.summary: Study reveals that pesticide poisoning kills 11,000 people each year, with India accounting for nearly 60% of fatalities Almost half of the world’s farmers are poisoned by pesticides every single year, a study has found. Using publicly available data from 2006-2023, the study, which was commissioned by Pesticide Action Network , found there to be an estimated 402-433m cases of unintentional acute pesticide poisoning of farmers and farm workers every year. stories.title: Floods killed dozens, but officials wore Prada and Balmain. Here’s why Filipinos are furious
stories.summary: Philippine officials, including President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and local politicians, faced public outrage for displaying wealth during deadly floods affecting millions. Corruption scandals revealed billions lost in flood control funds, with some projects substandard or never built, worsening flood impacts. Experts urge Filipinos to demand accountability, support new leaders, and push for better flood management policies to prevent future disasters. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr was standing onstage, microphone in hand, singing a love song to his wife. The scene was from an Aug 26 birthday celebration for First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos at their home in Makati City, beside the capital Manila. But by the time videos of it spread online days later, persistent monsoon rains had inundated communities across the main island of Luzon, leaving dozens dead and millions affected. The contrast quickly drew anger online. “That’s my president. He doesn’t care about the plight of the poor as long as (he) can party the night away,” commented Facebook user Joshua Javier Guitang in a repost of the video by local news agency NewsWatchPlus. The backlash reflects how a widening corruption scandal over billions of pesos in flood control spending has sharpened public scrutiny of the country’s political elite, with displays of comfort and wealth increasingly seen not merely as poor optics, but as symbols of a deeper failure of governance. Days later, in flood-hit Pampanga province north of Manila, Governor Lilia Pineda, Vice-Governor Dennis Pineda and San Fernando Mayor Vilma Caluag were photographed inspecting affected communities while wearing clothes and rain gear from luxury brands like Prada, Balmain and Burberry. The politicians’ outfits, including jackets costing tens of thousands of pesos, became targets of online ridicule.

stories.title: Indonesian officials say government-supplied meals tested after more than 500 students fall ill
stories.summary: Over 500 students in East Java were hospitalised with suspected food poisoning from government-supplied meals, prompting an investigation and meal sample testing by police. The free-meals programme, launched in 2025 to fight under-nutrition, has faced many issues including food poisoning, corruption, leadership changes, and high costs. The National Nutrition Agency is reforming the programme by shutting down kitchens violating standards, amid public dissatisfaction and concerns over food safety and fiscal impact. More than 500 students in Indonesia’s East Java were hospitalised with food poisoning suspected to have been caused by state-supplied meals, regional officials said on Sept 2, as the government works to reform the agency overseeing its ambitious free-meals scheme. President Prabowo Subianto launched his multibillion-dollar programme in 2025 to eradicate under-nutrition by giving free meals to tens of millions of children, but the scheme has suffered from controversies such as food poisoning, corruption allegations, leadership changes and a burdensome price tag. In East Java’s Sidoarjo region, more than 500 students fell ill on Sept 1, East Java deputy governor Emil Dardak told news channel Kompas TV. He said the National Nutrition Agency, which oversees the free-meals programme, was looking into whether the cause was the lunch the students had eaten. Subandi, the head of the local government in Sidoarjo, said most of the 516 students treated at hospital have been discharged. Subandi, who goes by one name, said police had taken samples from the meals as part of the investigation. There have been cases of mass food poisoning linked to the scheme. Non-governmental watchdog Network for Education Watch said that as of Aug 8, there had been some 37,600 cases of food poisoning linked to the programme. Improper food storage and late delivery of cooked meals are often to blame for the food poisoning, authorities have said.

stories.title: South Korea jails disabled care home head for sexually assaulting residents
stories.summary: A South Korean court has jailed the former head of a disabled care home for sexually assaulting multiple residents, in a case that shocked the nation. The man, surnamed Kim, was handed a 15-year prison term for abusing three residents at the Saekdongwon facility in Incheon City, west of Seoul. Police started investigating Kim after one of his victims, a woman with a severe intellectual disability, came forward in February last year. The case has prompted the government to inspect 1,507 care facilities for disabled people across the country, where 33 cases of suspected abuse were found. South Korean Prime Minister Kim Min-seok had described the abuse at Saekdongwon as "a grave matter that calls into question the very reason for the state's existence". An in-depth assessment of residents commissioned by Ganghwa County found that 20 current and former female residents may have experienced sexual abuse. Many in South Korea have asked how such a case could still occur, especially after laws were strengthened in 2011 to protect people with disabilities from sexual assault. Some have also raised questions on how the director's actions could have gone undetected for so long. Ganghwa County has ordered Saekdongwon to close, while Incheon City officials revoked the licence of the foundation that operated it. However, the closure has been deferred until the remaining residents have been relocated and arrangements for independent living have been completed. The foundation has filed an administrative lawsuit challenging the revocation of its licence.

stories.title: Mark to drop 1st solo project after leaving NCT
stories.summary: SEOUL, Sept. 2 (Yonhap) -- Mark, the rapper and singer who rose to fame as a mem...
article_sentences: Mark, the rapper and singer who rose to fame as a member of K-pop boy group NCT, will release his first solo single since leaving the band, his new agency.
Upper Room said Wednesday.

The track, "My Friend," will come out on Sept. 10 at 1 p.m. (Korean time), marking the artist's first new release in 17 months and his first public appearance as a solo act since departing NCT 127 and NCT Dream in April.

Mark debuted in 2016 as part of SM Entertainment's rotational supergroup NCT, quickly becoming one of the act's most prominent members through his appearances in multiple subunits, including NCT 127 and NCT Dream.

After nearly a decade with the company, he chose not to renew his exclusive contract and instead founded Upper Room, a one-person agency he describes as a "creative company" built with long-time collaborators he trusts.
He currently serves as a co-chief executive of the company.
